A1.evidence: I chose the advertised Glowkelp route in independent normal-speed WebKit exploration: 30 units at 52 cost 1,560, leaving 940; Copperhook arrival price was 86 rather than the observed 102. Selling returned 2,580. I opened Fogmouth details and saw risk 4/5, specialty goods and explicitly aged quotes. The full touch traveller changed cargo and routes across 30 nights; depth, fleet demand and debt repayment compete with buying.
below_10: The prominent best-known route is a useful starting point but does not compare whole-load proceeds after depth, risk and travel time; that comparison remains manual.

A2.evidence: I ran the frozen four-policy comparison on 16 matched seeds each. Informed median was about 605.9k, greedy 52.0k; whisper-spam beat informed on only 1/16 seeds. Its 4,750 trade-and-undo probes found zero profitable loops. Source inspection confirmed integrated pressure pricing with buy rounding up and sale rounding down. Touch seed 109 carried debt into night 11 and paid it off before night 12, visibly preserving early pressure.
below_10: The fixed fleet calendar becomes learnable across runs. The 16-seed sample does not establish that multiple equally strong endgame strategies exist.

A3.evidence: I inspected the touch-run Gull Gang card: 24% escape attempts, 22% fighting volleys, 60% enemy retaliation, cargo loss and a 491 toll were explicit. The leak fixture card offered an 11,400 patch versus jettisoning Moon Ink with usual value 19,000. All 16 WebKit/Chromium event fixtures passed, including success, failure, sinking, capped payment, resource conservation and committed offers after reload.
below_10: Combat percentages are per attempt or volley, so the overall expected cost of a multi-round fight is harder to compare with a single toll. Fixture coverage concentrates on gull and leak events, not every encounter permutation.

A4.evidence: The complete touch run moved from 2,500 cash and 6,000 debt through a night-12 debt-free milestone and later higher-value cargo to night-30 settlement. I personally completed an unaccelerated opening trade and voyage. A separate normal-speed Chromium voyage took 2,641ms; its median frame interval was 16.7ms.
below_10: The core sell/buy/map/confirm cycle repeats throughout the middle game. Full completion used FAST and reduced motion, so I cannot substantiate the duration or sustained feel of a full normal-speed run.

A5.evidence: I stepped through all five onboarding cards and opened the first trade sheet without external gameplay instructions. It showed the best observed sale, total, purse and hold after purchase, dealer depth, reserve policy and price history. I checked Fogmouth details showing one-night-old quotes and risk. The regression ending explained 566,691 cash plus 52,684 bank equals 619,375 final fortune, with debt paid and cargo zero.
below_10: Onboarding is a five-card explanation rather than a guided executed trade. Usual-price percentages and observed destination upside are different comparisons that a new player must distinguish.

B1.evidence: I inspected title, market, trade sheet, illustrated map, Gull Gang, leak and ending screenshots. Indigo water, amber lanterns, mint buying accents, illustrated district buildings and themed goods remain consistent. The ending rank emblem and restrained canal prose belong to the same setting.
below_10: Trade and port-detail sheets are predominantly dense text panels; their visual character depends more on palette and icons than the distinctive geography of the map.

B2.evidence: On the 390x844 market and 430x932 screenshot I could read purse, debt, hold and hull above per-good sparklines. The independent purchase showed 30 held at average 52, +65% at the destination price 86; the sale sheet confirmed total 2,580. Surge/glut and no-dealer labels distinguish price conditions. I inspected the desktop comparison layout too.
below_10: At 390x664 only roughly five goods fit at once, requiring a scroll to compare the expensive goods. Small sparklines communicate direction; precise history and full quotes require opening a sheet.

B3.evidence: I observed buy/sell feedback and an unaccelerated voyage in independent exploration, and inspected staged encounter art and settlement. Reading Sound verified separate synthesized buy, sell, profit, travel, encounter, damage, bank, upgrade, win and loss recipes. My real Chromium touch test created a running AudioContext in touchend; mute suspended it, and unmute resumed it in click without errors.
below_10: I did not hear the sound, so timbre, mix and fatigue are unassessed. Windows WebKit uses the disclosed gesture-policy stand-in. Accelerated full play does not establish that every animation stays unobtrusive over a normal-speed run.

B4.evidence: I selected Copperhook and sailed via the illustrated canal map, then selected Fogmouth and opened its details. I inspected selected-map screenshots at 360x640 and 390x664: seven recognizable ports, current location, route, one-night cost, danger, fleet marker and sale hint fit above navigation. Repeated destination selection passed at all required widths.
below_10: Compact route hints truncate at the shortest width; complete market and service information needs the separate details sheet.

B5.evidence: All four required WebKit sizes and 1280x800 Chromium passed touch/mouse, input, repeated-port, focus trap, inert-background and no-overflow checks. I inspected representative screenshots at every required size. My independent 390x664 audit found zero targets under 44px, zero text under 15px, zero approximate contrast failures and zero horizontal overflow. Source includes reduced-motion handling and keyboard shortcuts.
below_10: The bulletin button and route suggestion have a measured 4px gap. Contrast checking approximates gradients. Physical iPhone chrome, software keyboard, safe areas and silent switch were not tested; keyboard checks cover interactions and focus but not a complete keyboard-only game.

C1.evidence: Runtime evidence covers 30 nights, seven visual destinations, eight goods with changing prices, limited/upgradable hold, compounding debt and repayment, interest-bearing vault, multiple purchases, encounters with choices, settlement and persistent ledger. I inspected the event table, which exceeds eight distinct events. Phone/desktop presentation, charts, touch/mouse/keyboard interactions and real Chromium synthesized audio context all work in sampled tests.
below_10: Complete keyboard-only play and audible quality were not personally verified. Not every event and upgrade tier was exercised through actual UI taps; some coverage is function-driven simulation and explicit fixtures.

C2.evidence: I verified the exact 249,618-byte SHA256 and all 43 frozen helper hashes. Source search found only guarded localStorage access in the wrapper and no network APIs or external resources; the frozen source-constraint check passed. File URL touch play ran offline with no HTTP(S) requests. The restricted allow-scripts sandbox started successfully while localStorage access was confirmed blocked. CSS, JavaScript and art are inline and vanilla.

C3.evidence: The seed-109 real-touch run reached night-30 settlement with clean error/network logs. Separate function-driven seeds 100002 and 100003 reached settlement with fortunes 81,678 and 619,375. All eight verification groups and 16 event fixtures passed, including no-dealer input, repeated map selection, modal focus, corrupt saves, unavailable storage and sinking. Independent normal-speed trade/travel and Chromium mute testing also produced no errors.

C4.evidence: I typed -5 and 999999999 into the real trade input: the quote clamped respectively to zero and the legal 30-unit hold, without negative cash or excess cargo. My 1,560 purchase left 940; the 2,580 sale produced 3,520; debt compounded from 6,000 to 6,360 after one night. Regression settlement arithmetic checked exactly, high scores survived reload, corrupt saves/scores recovered, and all 4,750 split/alternating/ordinary round-trip probes were nonprofitable. Sixteen event fixtures confirmed payment/cargo conservation and reload commitment. Source inspection confirmed half-value cargo settlement and guarded numeric save validation.

C5.evidence: I inspected separated constants/data tables, market-depth quote functions, central S state, storage validation, input delegation and the isolated market/event RNG streams. My profile run sampled 156 frames on a 2,641ms normal voyage: median 16.7ms, p95 16.8ms, max 33.4ms. Forty fixture restarts kept listeners at 32 and documents at one; nodes changed by -2, collected heap by +97,436 bytes, with no errors.
below_10: Many functions are compressed into long lines, and DOM handlers, rendering and simulation share mutable globals. The lifecycle sample covers 40 direct restarts, not a long-session memory soak or physical-phone performance.

strengths: Clean complete touch game plus two complete function-driven regression games.
Integrated market depth resisted all 4,750 sampled round-trip probes.
Restricted sandbox and corrupt-storage recovery work; game is fully self-contained.
Distinct map art, readable trade quotes and explicit encounter stakes.
weaknesses: Small phone requires scrolling across the goods list and secondary detail sheets.
Four-pixel gap between bulletin and route controls is tighter than adjacent controls.
Compressed functions and global state increase maintenance effort.
Audible quality, physical iPhone behavior and full normal-speed pacing remain unverified.

evidence.phone_notes: Primary automated actual-touch WebKit seed 109 at 390x844 completed all 30 nights; FAST/reduced motion accelerates animation only. Independent normal-speed exploration completed onboarding and a buy/sail/sell cycle, tested typed boundary quantities, and inspected Fogmouth details. Frozen tests cover 390x844, 390x664, 360x640 and 430x932. Human-style judgment here means my inspection and chosen actions, not a human participant or physical-device trial.
evidence.desktop_notes: 1280x800 Chromium runtime and screenshot checks passed; two full function-driven regression games completed. Simulations and fixtures are separate from scored touch play.
evidence.audio_notes: Real Chromium context running -> suspended on mute -> running on unmute, no errors. Windows WebKit stand-in only tests gesture policy. No listening test or physical-iPhone audio claim.
coverage_limits: No physical device or audible listening test.
Only opening exploration and one diagnostic voyage used normal timing; full UI run used FAST/reduced motion.
Second and third complete games used actual game functions, not touch.
No complete keyboard-only run; no claim of exhaustive event, seed or exploit coverage.
execution_issues: T3 preview rejected file URL as unsupported-protocol: file:; supplied Playwright harness used instead.
One 500ms onboarding step could not yet find Next; retry with 1500ms completed the tour. This was consistent with documented Windows WebKit animation throttling, not a demonstrated game soft-lock.

verdict: Technically robust, complete and visually coherent. No rubric cap or confirmed gameplay defect was triggered; the main reservations are dense small-screen details, maintainability and explicitly limited audio/device/pacing coverage.
